chunks: 915 - It is narrated from Ḥammād ibn ‘Īsā that he said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام said to me one day, “Do you know how to perform salat (prayer), O Ḥammād?” He said: I said, “My master, I have memorized the book of Ḥarīz concerning salat (prayer).” He said: So he عليه السلام said, “No matter, stand and pray.” He said: So I stood before him, facing the qiblah, and I began the salat (prayer), and performed ruku‘ and sajdah. Then he said, “O Ḥammād, you do not know how to perform salat (prayer). How ugly it is for a man that sixty years or seventy years pass over him, yet he does not establish even one salat (prayer) with its limits complete.” Ḥammād said: So humiliation struck me within myself, and I said, “May I be made your ransom, then teach me the salat (prayer).”

Then Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام stood facing the qiblah, upright. He let both his hands hang upon his thighs, having joined his fingers together, and he brought his feet near each other until there were three spread fingers between them. He faced with the toes of both his feet together and did not turn them away from the qiblah, in humility and stillness, and he said: “Allāhu Akbar.” Then he recited al-Ḥamd with measured recitation, and “Qul huwa Allāhu Aḥad.” Then he paused a little, for the measure of one breathing while standing. Then he said, “Allāhu Akbar,” while standing; then he performed ruku‘, and filled his palms from his knees with the fingers spread, and pushed his knees back until his back became level, such that if a drop of water or oil were poured upon it, it would not move because of the levelness of his back. He pushed his knees back, straightened his neck, and closed his eyes. Then he glorified three times with measured recitation and said: “Subḥāna Rabbīya al-‘Aẓīmi wa biḥamdih.” Then he stood upright; and when he had become settled in standing, he said: “Sami‘a Allāhu liman ḥamidah.” Then he said the takbīr while standing, raised his hands opposite his face, and performed sajdah, placing his hands on the ground before his knees. Then he said: “Subḥāna Rabbīya al-A‘lā wa biḥamdih” three times. He did not place any part of his body upon another part of it, and he performed sajdah upon eight bones: the forehead, the two palms, the two knee-caps, the tips of the two big toes, and the nose. So these seven are obligatory, and placing the nose upon the ground is sunnah, and that is al-irghām. Then he raised his head from sajdah, and when he had sat upright, he said: “Allāhu Akbar.” Then he sat upon his left side, and placed the outer part of his right foot upon the inner part of his left foot, and said: “Astaghfiru Allāha Rabbī wa atūbu ilayh.” Then he said the takbīr while sitting, and performed the second sajdah, and said as he had said in the first. He did not use any part of his body to support another part of it in ruku‘ or sajdah, and he kept his arms outspread, and did not place his forearms on the ground. Then he performed two rak‘ahs in this manner.
Then he said: “O Ḥammād, pray like this.”

key_terms.أَسْتَغْفِرُ: I seek forgiveness, a formula of repentance said between the prostrations
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being taught in detail
key_terms.بِخُشُوعٍ: with humility and inward reverence during worship
key_terms.رَكَعَ: he performed ruku‘, the bowing posture in salat (prayer)
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: an established recommended practice, as distinct from what is obligatory
key_terms.فَرْضٌ: obligatory requirement in the act of worship

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام teach the correct way to perform salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the detailed manner of performing salat (prayer) as demonstrated by Imam Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام to Ḥammād ibn ‘Īsā. It emphasizes precision, humility, composure, and fulfilling the prescribed limits of salat (prayer) correctly. It is an important source in Shia discussions of the form and etiquette of prayer.
